rationale: C01 is the closest in form because it also presents a brief covering letter enclosing a longer presidential letter, but that is routine correspondence machinery and the substantive arguments, purpose, and operative content do not correspond. C06 shares the immediate Korean-war and military context and includes presidential clarification of a previously stated position, while C10 praises military service and mentions the Joint Chiefs of Staff; neither shares distinctive language, an operative sequence, or sufficiently similar administrative machinery with the child's apology and defense of the Marine Corps. No candidate plausibly supplied a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have this date addressed a letter to the Commandant of the Marine Corps, a copy of which I am enclosing.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am enclosing herewith a copy of a letter which I am sending to Senator Tydings
shared_material.explanation: C01 shares the cover-letter-and-enclosure format, but this is a routine correspondence device and the enclosed letters serve materially different purposes.

shared_material.child_excerpt: What I had in mind at the time this letter was written was the specific question raised by Mr. McDonough
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To the end that there be no misunderstanding concerning the position of the Government of the United States with respect to Formosa
shared_material.explanation: C06 likewise clarifies an earlier position, but the language and argumentative structure are not close enough to establish reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am profoundly aware of the magnificent history of the United States Marine Corps, and of the many heroic deeds of the Marines
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The nation is extremely fortunate to have had the benefit of this most recent service by you.
shared_material.explanation: C10 contains military commendation, but only at a broad and conventional level.
